title: Refine streaming slot allocator to balance mixed prompt/response distributions
creator: Asha Patel
description: We are observing elevated 95th/99th tail latencies and periodic GPU memory pressure when serving mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts with long responses and vice versa). Current continuous-batcher slot allocator favors throughput but leaves hot KV residency and fragmentation that spikes memory usage under skew. This ticket refactors the streaming slot allocator to: 1) introduce a short/long affinity window that biases slot admission for heterogeneous sequences; 2) add a decaying KV residency policy so long-responses do not permanently pin slots; 3) integrate a lightweight slab compaction signal to prompt preemptive coalescing when fragmentation threatens >85% slab use. Goal is to lower tail latency variability and reduce eviction storms that cause SLO breaches for enterprise Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for mixed synthetic workload (MixA dataset) <= 120ms under 70% p99 throughput for 30m
P99 latency regression < 10% compared to baseline under steady-state 60% util
No GPU OOMs or eviction storms in a 3-hour soak test with mixed dialogs (100k requests);
KV cache average residency reduction >= 18% for long-response-heavy traces compared to baseline
Feature flag gated rollout with canary path and automatic fallback to old allocator

rollback_plan: Feature flag default off. Canary rollout for internal-only first 24h. If p95 increases >10% or error rate >1% relative to baseline during canary, flip flag off and hotfix will be prepared. For OOMs, immediate rollback and CPU-only fallback for affected tenants.
notes: Key trade-offs discussed: aggressive eviction reduces memory pressure but increases recompute/KV warmup cost; decided to use probabilistic short/long admission plus decay to avoid repeated full-evict cycles. Future follow-ups: 1) per-tenant policy tuning, 2) integrate quantization-aware residency heuristics, 3) explore GPU-side slab compaction primitives when supported by drivers.
